1.title: CDMP FUNDAMENTALS
1.text: Welcome, and congratulations on taking the first step toward becoming a Certified Data Management Professional. This course is your complete, structured path to passing the CDMP Fundamentals exam, which is based entirely on the DAMA-DMBOK Second Edition. Over the next fourteen modules, we'll work through every knowledge area the exam tests — clearly, efficiently, and with a constant eye on what actually shows up on test day. Let's get started.

1.title: Welcome — Let's Get You Certified
1.text: Before we dive in, a quick word about why this course exists. I sat the CDMP Fundamentals exam and passed it with a score above eighty percent — the threshold that qualifies for the Master tier. So everything you're about to learn is shaped by real exam experience, not just theory. Here's my promise to you: I won't just walk you through the DMBOK content. I'll show you exactly what the exam tests, how it phrases its questions, and where candidates trip up. That insider perspective is the difference between knowing the material and passing the exam. Let's make sure you do both.

1.title: Is This Course for You?
1.text: So, is this course right for you? If you work with data in almost any capacity — as an analyst, an engineer, an architect, a database administrator, a governance or quality specialist, or a BI professional — this is built for you. It's equally valuable if you're a business analyst, a project manager, or a student looking to break into the data field and prove your knowledge with a respected, vendor-neutral credential. You don't need any prior certification; the Fundamentals exam has no prerequisites. What you do need is a few focused hours each week and a willingness to learn the DMBOK's specific vocabulary. If that's you, you're in exactly the right place.

1.title: 14 DMBOK2 Knowledge Areas You Must Master
1.text: Here's the full scope of what we'll cover: the fourteen knowledge areas of the DMBOK Second Edition. We start with Data Management itself, then move through Data Ethics, Governance, Architecture, Modeling and Design, Storage and Operations, Security, Integration and Interoperability, Document and Content Management, Reference and Master Data, Data Warehousing and Business Intelligence, Metadata, Data Quality, and finally Big Data and Data Science. Each one becomes a dedicated module. Now, the wheel on your screen is the famous DAMA Wheel — it places Data Governance right at the hub, with ten knowledge areas arranged around it. Our course wraps three more chapters around those eleven — the Data Management overview, Data Ethics, and Big Data — to reach fourteen in total. Together they map one-to-one onto the exam blueprint — so when you finish this course, you'll have covered everything the exam can ask.

1.title: Every Module Follows the Same Proven Pattern
1.text: Every module in this course follows the same proven rhythm, so you always know what to expect. Follow the flow on screen: we begin with the formal definition and goals, move into the core frameworks and models, then cover the activities, roles, tools, and metrics, and we finish by calling out the common exam traps. Then — and this is important — every single module ends with five exam-style practice questions drawn from real practice pools, so you can test yourself immediately. Throughout, you'll see "Exam Tip" callouts; those flag the highest-probability test points, the things I'd bet money you'll see on the exam. And one more thing: the depth of each module is deliberately proportional to its exam weight. We'll spend far more time on the eleven-percent chapters than on the two-percent ones — which brings us to the certification itself.

1.title: What Is the CDMP?
1.text: Let's define what you're actually earning. The CDMP — Certified Data Management Professional — is the leading professional certification in the data management field, administered by DAMA International, the Data Management Association. What makes it credible is that it's built entirely on the DAMA-DMBOK Second Edition, published in 2017. That's the "Data Management Body of Knowledge" — the closest thing our profession has to a universal reference text. The certification is vendor-neutral, globally recognized, and it validates your knowledge across all fourteen DMBOK chapters. In fact, the DMBOK itself explicitly names the CDMP as the exam it supports. So when you study the book, you're studying the exam.

1.title: One Exam, Four Credential Tiers
1.text: Now here's something that surprises a lot of candidates: there's essentially one exam, but four credential tiers — and you can see them climbing on screen. Pass the Fundamentals exam at sixty percent or above, and you earn the Associate credential. Score seventy percent or higher, and — combined with two specialist exams and some years of experience — you become eligible for the Practitioner tier. Hit eighty percent, plus the specialist exams and more experience, and you're on track for Master. The top tier, Fellow, isn't earned by exam at all — it's awarded by nomination for distinguished, long-term contributions to the profession. Here's the key takeaway, and write this down: your score on this single Fundamentals exam determines which tiers you qualify for. That's why I always say — aim high. A strong score keeps every door open for the rest of your career.

1.title: The Fundamentals Exam at a Glance
1.text: Let's demystify the exam format, because knowing it removes a lot of anxiety. You'll face one hundred multiple-choice questions, each with a single best answer chosen from four options. You get ninety minutes. If English isn't your first language, you can request an accommodation — typically an extra twenty minutes and the use of a printed language dictionary. Now, here's the part people love: it's an open-book exam. You're allowed to reference the DMBOK Second Edition, in print or e-book form, while you test. The exam is delivered online with a remote proctor, and you'll see your result when you finish. One quick bit of math: ninety minutes across one hundred questions is about fifty-four seconds per question. That pace matters, and we'll talk strategy for it shortly.

1.title: Exam Content Blueprint — Where the 100 Questions Come From
1.text: This slide is one you'll want to come back to, because it tells you where to invest your study time. Look at the bar chart: the hundred questions aren't spread evenly across the chapters — the bars make the imbalance obvious at a glance. Six knowledge areas dominate. Data Governance, Data Quality, Data Modeling and Design, and Metadata each carry about eleven percent — that's your "big four," and together they're forty-four percent of the entire exam. Add Reference and Master Data and Data Warehousing and BI, each around ten percent, and you're looking at roughly sixty-four percent of the exam coming from just six chapters. The middle tier — Architecture, Security, Storage, Integration, and Document and Content Management — sits at about six percent each. And three foundational chapters — Data Management, Data Ethics, and Big Data — are two percent apiece. The lesson is simple: don't give every chapter equal time. Weight your effort toward the heavy hitters.

1.title: What 'Passing' Really Means — Score Thresholds
1.text: Let's be crystal clear about what passing means — and the coloured scale on screen lays it out band by band. Below sixty percent, you're not yet certified — but you can retake. Land between sixty and sixty-nine percent, and you've earned the CDMP Associate. Reach seventy to seventy-nine, and you're Associate-certified and Practitioner-eligible. Eighty percent or above, and you've opened the door to the Master tier. Here's my advice, even if you only need the Associate credential: target seventy percent or higher. Why? Because it gives you a comfortable safety margin on exam day, and it future-proofs your certification in case you decide to pursue the higher tiers later. Aim for the score you'll wish you had, not the minimum you can scrape by with.

1.title: Registration & Logistics
1.text: A few practical notes on actually booking the exam. You register through DAMA International's official CDMP portal. The exam is taken online with a remote proctor watching through your webcam, so you'll need stable internet and a quiet, private room. Have your DMBOK Second Edition on hand, since it's open book. And if things don't go your way the first time, you can retake it — there's a waiting period and an additional fee. One important caveat, shown right here on the slide: exam fees, scheduling, identification requirements, and retake policies do change over time. So before you book, always confirm the current details on the official DAMA website. Don't take any dollar figure or policy as permanent — verify it.

1.title: Open Book ≠ No Preparation
1.text: The open-book format is a genuine advantage — but only if you use it correctly, and many candidates misuse it. Here's the trap: people assume "open book" means they don't have to study. That's a fast way to fail. Remember, you have about fifty-four seconds per question. You simply don't have time to look up more than a handful of answers. So here's how to use the book well. First, know its structure cold, so you can flip to the right section in seconds. Second, tab and bookmark the key tables — the definitions, the principles, the DAMA Wheel. And third, use the book to confirm an answer you're unsure about, not to learn the material for the first time. Think of the DMBOK as a safety net for five or ten genuinely tough questions — not as a replacement for preparation. Study first; the book is your backup.

1.title: Your 6-Step Study Strategy
1.text: Let me give you a concrete, repeatable study loop you can run for every chapter — it's the circle you see on screen, and you run it once per chapter. Step one: watch the module here in this course. Step two: read the corresponding chapter summary to reinforce the key points while they're fresh. Step three: memorize the anchors — the definitions, the numbered lists, the acronyms — because the exam tests these precisely. Step four: do the five practice questions at the end of each module, then progress to full-length practice exams. Step five — and this is the one people skip — review your wrong answers and understand why you got them wrong; don't just memorize the right letter. And step six: spend a little time mapping the DMBOK so you can find facts fast during the open-book exam. Run that loop, weighted toward the heavy chapters, and you'll be ready.

1.title: High-Yield Memory Anchors & Acronyms
1.text: The CDMP exam has a real fondness for precise lists and acronyms, so let's arm you with the highest-yield ones up front. SMART — Specific, Measurable, Actionable, Realistic, Time-bound — describes good objectives. DIKW is the Data, Information, Knowledge, Wisdom pyramid. ROT stands for Redundant, Obsolete, and Trivial data, the kind you want to minimize. P-D-C-O — Plan, Develop, Control, Operate — are the four activity categories used across every knowledge area. ADKAR — Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability, Reinforcement — comes from change management. GAIP is the Generally Accepted Information Principles. And SIPOC — Suppliers, Inputs, Process, Outputs, Consumers — is the basis for the DMBOK context diagrams. Here's a crucial exam tip: when a list has a named count, like "the six goals" or "the eleven principles," the exam loves to ask which item is NOT one of them. So don't half-learn these lists — memorize the complete set.

1.title: Exam-Day Technique — Score Every Point You Can
1.text: Let's talk tactics for the exam itself, because good technique can be worth several points. First, budget your time — about fifty-four seconds per question — and never let a single tough question swallow five minutes. Use a two-pass approach: answer all the easy questions first, flag the hard ones, and circle back with whatever time remains. When you're unsure, eliminate the obviously wrong choices to improve your odds. And always, always answer every question — there's no penalty for guessing, so a blank is just a wasted chance. Finally, read the entire question stem and watch for qualifier words like BEST, MOST, NOT, and EXCEPT, which completely change what's being asked. And when two answers both look correct, choose the one that uses the DMBOK's exact wording. That tiebreaker wins more often than you'd think.

1.title: Common Traps & Red-Flag Words
1.text: Now let me show you where candidates routinely lose easy marks, so you don't. The single most common trap is confusing Data Governance with Data Management. Governance is oversight — it ensures data is managed properly. Management is execution — it actually does the work. The exam tests that distinction constantly. Another trap: mixing up the three operating models — Centralized, Replicated, and Federated. A third: confusing the different steward types and how much authority each one has. And a classic one — treating the data lifecycle as if it's the systems development lifecycle. It isn't; it's based on the product lifecycle. Finally, watch for red-flag absolute words: "always," "never," "only," "all," "none," "exclusively." The DMBOK favors balanced, qualified statements, so an answer with an absolute is frequently — though not always — a distractor. Read those carefully.

1.title: How to Use This Course
1.text: A few tips to get maximum value from these modules. The first time through, follow them in order — later chapters genuinely build on concepts from earlier ones. As you watch, pause and say the definitions out loud; the scripts are written to be spoken, and speaking them helps them stick. After each module, attempt the five practice questions cold, before you review the answers — that tells you what you truly know versus what just felt familiar. Revisit the big-weight chapters — Governance, Modeling, Metadata, and Data Quality — at least twice. And keep a personal cheat sheet of the numbers and lists as you go; building it yourself is one of the best ways to lock them into memory. Every module's script file gives you the exact narration for every slide, so you can study by listening too.

1.title: What's Next — Module 1: Data Management
1.text: Alright — orientation done. You now know the exam, the blueprint, the scoring, and the strategy. It's time to start learning the material itself. In Module 1, we tackle Data Management: the formal definition you'll see quoted on the exam, the eleven data management principles, the DAMA Wheel that organizes the entire body of knowledge, and the data lifecycle that explains why data is such a unique asset. Master this foundational chapter, and the whole DMBOK framework clicks into place. I'll see you in Module 1.
